attempt_4_hypothesis.hypothesis: Direct accesses to the Settings global, instead of an explicit long-lived Settings pointer local, might allow MWCC to retain the owner in r31 while independently assigning the global base to r30.

trials.variant: replace the Settings pointer local with direct lbl_8031D3B8 field accesses
trials.result: MWCC retained the owner in the desired r31, but did not retain the Settings address in r30; repeated address formation changed the function shape and regressed the score

trials.variant: restore the Settings pointer and reverse the two initialized local declaration lines
trials.result: byte-identical to the incumbent, showing declaration order does not alter MWCC's virtual-register allocation

Material relocation types, targets, and addends agree; all addends are zero. The four R_PPC_NONE annotations on each side target lbl_8031D3B8 with addends 0, 0, 40, and 20.

divergence: The size and control flow are exact. Retail retains the owner Work pointer in r31 and lbl_8031D3B8 in r30; generated code retains them in r30 and r31. This swaps the prologue/addi schedule and all owner/global field bases. The same allocation decision changes the signed remainder scheduling: retail uses r5/r4/r7/r6 for the multiplier constant, angle, mulhw result, and shifted quotient, while generated uses r4/r5/r0/r0 before the final r6 sign adjustment.
